previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of hypertension, SIADH, aortic stenosis, and chronic rotator cuff tears was admitted after being found hypotensive with a rapid heart rate of 140, briefly in atrial fibrillation that resolved spontaneously. The episode followed a recent sacroiliac joint injection known to cause labile blood pressure in this patient. He had been on escalating doses of valsartan, most recently 160 mg twice daily, and was noted to have hyponatremia (sodium 125) on admission. Chest imaging showed mild interstitial edema likely due to transient flash pulmonary edema from the arrhythmia. He was managed with IV fluids, holding valsartan, and continuing metoprolol for rate control. His sodium normalized, blood pressure stabilized, and he remained in sinus rhythm. Advair was discontinued due to potential contribution from salmeterol to arrhythmia risk. He was discharged home with modified medications and plans for outpatient follow-up.
